data.summary: ddflow_bug_found's MCP param evidence (declared help: 'What showed the bug: a command') is passed as repro_cmd (surfaces/declared/records.py:193) and services/reprobundle.py:345 RC.check runs it through the shell in a scratch checkout. The CLI help for --repro-cmd says 'kept in the repro bundle (never run)' (records.py:247). Probe in a throwaway repo, 2026-11-05: --repro-cmd and an MCP evidence value each created a marker file OUTSIDE the scratch tree, and a host variable set before the call was echoed into the stored output tail, so the run has the full filesystem and environment. reprocheck.py's docstring calls it 'the operator's own command', but over MCP an agent supplies it; a lane held to its globs by hooks can run a shell through it; D-research-flows-r2 and D-research-system keep agent-proposed commands inert until a digest approval. Wanted: correct the help; gate execution of agent-supplied commands (digest approval or the SEC-sandbox class), or store them unexecuted; evidence text not meant as a command must not run.
data.title: bug found runs an agent-supplied repro command through the shell with the host environment, while its help says never run

data.summary: [bugs] repro_env defaults include 'CLAUDE*' (config_sections/bugs.py:82-91). Only names that look secret are masked, so CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_OWNER_ACCOUNT_UUID, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_OWNER_ORG_UUID and the messaging socket path are stored as values and printed by ddflow show. Bundles are committed blobs: count-only git grep, 2026-11-05: 755 of 845 tracked .ddflow/blobs files at HEAD carry the account UUID variable with a UUID value; 392 blobs at origin/main carry the variable, so it has left this machine. Neither is a credential, but it is operator identity leaving the project without recorded consent (r-consent-outward). Wanted: narrow the default to the variables that explain behaviour (for example CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT) or mask values by default; ask the operator what to do with the blobs in history; a test that a bundle holds no account identifier.
data.title: Repro bundles commit the operator's account and org UUIDs: the default repro_env pattern CLAUDE* records them

data.budget: one read-only session, no test suite
data.claim: Built and wired: bisect (test-file polluter ddmin only, no commit bisect), bug repro bundle and repro-cmd run at a recorded sha, regression fail-before verify, gate verify mutation, verify, flake log, tests selection, recall, similar, research notes (verdict required at filing, immutable, no open-hypothesis state). 'ddflow probe' is a git merge-conflict probe and 'ddflow replay' rebuilds decision history from the log: neither is a debugging tool. Absent in code: any process isolation (no rlimit, namespace, seccomp, container call), any debugger, tracer, dump or binary tool, any kind or pipeline for an investigation (kind=research runs the full implementation pipeline). Planned but far: RE-debug-flow wave 35 with 242 open transitive needs, RF-ledger wave 22 with 118, RF-run wave 23 with 123, RE-accept wave 37 with 341 against the P-reimpl kill date 2026-12-03. Cheap roots exist: SEC-sandbox, TM-target, TM-defect-model, QA-f2p-task, DX-bug-repro-gate-and-mcp, DX-command-log, RE-decide are all wave 0 with no open needs. Decided without a task: debugger and disassembler MCP adapters (D-reimpl-answers point 4 appears only as a sentence in RE-ledger-ingest). New phases are under the D-scope-focus-2026-11 intake freeze until open tasks are under 1500 (2614 open).
data.falsifier: A code search finds a process-isolation call or a debugger or tracer integration in ddflow/, or RE-debug-flow has an open closure under 50, or a task body names a debugger adapter as its deliverable.
data.mechanism: The generally useful debug flow was filed as a template behind RS-templates, and RS-templates needs RF-docs, which needs every shipped flow (math, hw, dsp, ml, panel, delegate), so a small template inherits the whole research programme. Execution safety was deferred to SEC-sandbox, which three tracks (RE, TM, RQ) wait on and nobody has started. The research record stores conclusions, so a live hypothesis has nowhere to go until the reasoning log, itself behind P-decisions and P-org-config.
data.probe: ddflow --json list task (4593 rows, 5 pages) and list phase --limit 1000; open-closure script over needs plus inherited phase needs; ddflow waves --check; git grep -E 'unshare|bwrap|firejail|nsjail|seccomp|setrlimit|RLIMIT_|landlock' and 'gdb|lldb|pdb|strace|ltrace|debugpy|valgrind|py-spy|coredump|objdump|ghidra|radare|frida' over ddflow/; body scan of task events; read services/{bisect,probe,reprobundle,reprocheck,verify,flakes}.py and gates/mutation.py; throwaway repo probe of bug found --repro-cmd and MCP evidence.
data.probe_output: Isolation grep: only docker-run string matchers and doc text; jinja SandboxedEnvironment for templates only. Debugger grep over ddflow/: 0 hits. Waves check: 0 stale stamps. Closures: RE-debug-flow 242, RS-templates 241, RF-docs 240, RF-template 60, RF-ledger 118, RF-run 123, TF-flows-code 139, RE-sandbox-gate 67, TM-safety 65, SEC-hunt-engine 4, SEC-sandbox 0, TM-target 0, RE-accept 341. Tasks: 2614 open, 25 running, 3 blocked. Bugs 1459: reproduced recorded on 18 (16 yes, 2 no); 1026 of 1046 fixed carry a regression test. Research 1542: 1413 confirmed, 89 theoretical, 40 refuted. Flake log 49 lines. Probe: both markers written outside the scratch tree and a host variable appeared in the stored output (filed B18cd856a67).
data.question: What debugging, investigation, research, reverse-engineering and safe-execution capability does ddflow have and plan on 2026-11-05, and where are the gaps and hosts for new work?
